translations.text: [?] your sons as prophets for me, and from your grandchildren, priests for me. Are these not the children of [?], says the Lord?
And you gave wine to those who had purified themselves, and you commanded the prophets, saying, “Do not prophesy to us.”
Therefore, look: I will roll you about as a cart rolls when it is full of straw.
And the runner will not run away, and the strong man's strength will not make him secure, and the warrior will not be able to save his life.
And the archer will not be able to stand firm, and the swift-footed man will not save himself, nor will the horseman save his life.
And the courageous man, in his strength, will flee naked on that day, says the Lord.
Listen to this word that the Lord has spoken against you, house of [?], and against every tribe that I brought out of the land of Egypt, saying:
“You alone have I known among all the tribes of the earth. Therefore I will call you to account for your acts of violence.”
Will two people walk together without knowing each other at all?
Or will a lion cry out from its woodland when it has no prey there? Will a lion cub utter its voice at all from its den without having caught anything?
Will a bird fall to the ground without someone setting a trap for it? Will a trap open on the ground without catching anything?
Will a trumpet sound in a city without the people being alarmed? Will disaster happen in a city unless the Lord has caused it to happen?
For the Lord will not do anything without revealing his instruction to his servants, the prophets.
A lion will roar, and who will not be afraid? The Lord God has spoken, and who will not prophesy?

Proclaim it to the regions among the Assyrians and to the regions of Egypt, and say, “Gather on the mountain of Samaria and see the many astonishing things in its midst, and the oppression within it. Those who are mistreated [?] in its midst.”
And they did not know how to practice understanding, says the Lord—those who store up violence and misery for themselves in their regions.
Therefore this is what the Lord says: “Tyre will become desolate, along with the land around it, and he will bring your strength down from you, and your regions will be plundered.”

Therefore this is what the Lord says: “Just as a shepherd rescues two legs or a piece of an ear from a lion's mouth, so the children of [?] who live in Samaria will be rescued, before a tribe in Damascus, priests.”
Listen and bear witness to the house of Jacob, says the Lord, the God of hosts.
For on the day when I punish [?] for his sins, I will also punish the altars of Bethel, and the horns of the altar will be torn down and fall to the ground.

And I will shake the winter house and strike it down upon the house where people cool themselves in summer. The ivory houses will be destroyed, and many other houses will be added to them, says the Lord God.
Listen to this word, cows of Bashan who live on the mountain of Samaria, who oppress the poor and trample on those in distress, who say to their masters, “Give us wine to drink.”

The Lord God has sworn by his holy mountain: “Look, days are coming upon you when they will take you away with weapons, and those with you will be thrown into bronze cauldrons, with the locusts of pestilence burning beneath them.”
And they will bring you out, men and women, naked because of your fear of one another, and they will throw you onto Mount Remma, says the Lord God.
You went into Bethel and sinned, and you went into Gilgal and multiplied your lawlessness. And you bring your sacrifices in the morning and your tithes on the third day.
And they read the law outside and proclaimed confessions. Say, “These are the things you loved, children of [?], says the Lord.”
And I will give you a [?] of teeth in all your cities and a lack of bread in all your places. Yet you did not turn back to me, says the Lord.

And I withheld the rain three months before the harvest. I will send rain on one city, but I will not send rain on another city. One field will receive water, and the field on which I do not send rain will dry up.
Two or three cities will gather in one city to drink water, but they will not have enough to drink. Yet you did not return to me, says the Lord.
I struck you with scorching heat and jaundice, and you increased [?].
[?] But I am a cattle herder, and I prick sycamore figs.
And the Lord took me from among my sheep. The Lord said to me, “Go and prophesy to my people, [?].”
And now listen to the word of the Lord. You say, “Do not prophesy against [?], and do not gather a crowd against the house of Jacob.”

Therefore, this is what the Lord says: “Your wife will become a prostitute in the city, and your sons and daughters will fall by the sword. Your land will be measured out with a cord, and you will die in an unclean land. And [?] will be taken captive from its land.” This is how the Lord showed me.
And there was a container for trapping birds. The Lord said to me, “What do you see, Amos?” I said, “A container for trapping birds.”
The Lord said to me, “The end has come upon my people, [?]. I will no longer continue to spare them.”
And the temple ceilings will cry out with songs of mourning on that day, says the Lord. Great is the slaughter that has taken place. No one will raise their voice anywhere.
Listen, then, to these things, you who crush the afflicted in the morning and oppress the poor on the earth.

Those who say, “When will the month end, so that we can sell? And when will the Sabbath end, so that we can open our storehouse, make the grain measure small and the weight large, and make a dishonest balance?
Then we can acquire the afflicted for silver and the poor in exchange for sandals, and sell the refuse from every crop.”
The Lord has sworn by the pride of Jacob: “None of your deeds will ever be forgotten.”
Will the earth not tremble because of these things, and everyone living in it mourn? Their end will rise like a river, and they will sink like the river of Egypt.
And on that day, says the Lord, the sun will set at noon, and the light over the earth will become dark during the day.

I will turn your festivals into mourning and all your songs into lamentation. I will make everyone put sackcloth around their waist, and I will make everyone shave their head. I will make it like mourning for a loved one, and those with him like a day of anguish.
Look, days are coming, says the Lord, when I will send a famine upon the earth—not a famine of bread or a thirst for water, but a famine of hearing the word of the Lord.
And they will wander from sea to sea, and from the north to the east. They will run about searching for the word of the Lord, but they will not find it.
On that day the beautiful young women and the young men will faint from thirst.
Those who swear by the forgiveness of Samaria, saying, “As your god lives, Dan,” and, “As your god lives, Beersheba,” will fall and will no longer be able to rise.

I saw the Lord standing on the altar, and he said, “Strike the mercy seat so that the outer gateways shake, and strike everyone on the head. I will kill the rest of them with the sword. None of them will escape, and none of them will survive.
If they go up to heaven, I will bring them down from there. If they go down to the realm of the dead, my hand will pull them up from there.
If they hide on the summit of Carmel, I will pursue them there and bring them out. If they hide from my eyes in the depths of the sea, I will command the serpent there to bite them.
And if they go into captivity before their enemies, I will command the sword there to kill them. I will fix my eyes on them for harm and not for good.”
And the Lord God Almighty, who touches the earth and makes it shake, said: “All who live in it will mourn, and its end will rise like a river and sink like the river of Egypt.”
He builds his place of ascent in heaven and has established his promise on the earth. He calls for the water of the sea and pours it over the surface of the earth. The Lord Almighty is his name.
“Children of [?], are you not like the children of the Ethiopians to me?” said the Lord. “Did I not bring [?] out of Egypt, the Philistines out of Cappadocia, and the Syrians out of Kir?”

“Look, the eyes of the Lord are watching the kingdom of sinners, and I will remove them from the surface of the earth. Yet I will not completely remove the house of Jacob,” said the Lord. “For look, I myself will give the command.”
“And I will purify all the nations of [?], in the way silver is purified, so that none of them is destroyed on the earth.”
“All the sinners among the people will die by the sword, those who say, ‘Evils will not approach us or come upon us.’”
“On that day I will raise up David’s tent, which has fallen. I will rebuild the parts of it that have fallen, and I will raise up its ruined parts. I will rebuild it as it was in ancient days.”
So that the rest of humanity and all the nations over whom my name has been invoked may seek, says the Lord, who does these things.

“Look, days are coming,” said the Lord, “when the harvest will overtake the gathering, and the grapes will last until sowing time. The mountains will drip sweetness, and all the hills will sprout trees.”

“And I will bring my people [?] back from captivity. They will rebuild the ruined cities and live in them. They will plant vineyards and drink their wine, and they will plant gardens and eat their fruit.”
And I will plant them in their land, and from now on they will never be removed from their land, which I gave them, says the Lord God Almighty.
